sentences.text: For the State : Mrs. Anuradha Sahay, A.P.P.

2.  This anticipatory bail application under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, has been preferred by the petitioner apprehending his arrest in connection with Poraiyahat P.S. Case No.42 of 2023, for offences under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B IPC.
The case is presently pending before the Court of learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Godda.
3. Learned counsel representing the petitioner submits that only on the basis of confessional statement of one Alok Kumar Paswan, the petitioner has been made an accused.
It is the case of the petitioner that only on the basis of conjectures, the case has been instituted against this petitioner.

4. Learned A.P.P. representing the State opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail and submits that the petitioner impersonated and participated in the selection process of Home Guard in place of Alok Kumar Paswan, which Alok Kumar Paswan has accepted.
5. After going through the documents, I find that in the 2025:JHHC:14869 selection process of Home Guards in the physical test, this petitioner appeared in place of Alok Kumar Paswan.
When Alok Kumar Paswan was confronted, he accepted that it is this petitioner who has participated in the physical test and long distance running in place of Alok Kumar Paswan.
Lankesh Paswan vs The State Of Jharkhand.

6. Considering the nature of allegation, it is not a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to this petitioner,
as this case needs proper investigation, where the presence of petitioner is necessary.
7. With the aforesaid observation, this Anticipatory Bail Application stands dismissed.
(ANANDA SEN, J.) Prashant. Cp-3 Lankesh Paswan vs The State Of Jharkhand.
